posts.title: Armed Forces Family Fun Day
posts.summary:
On 27 June, Pat Midgley Community Hub was delighted to host an Armed Forces Day Family Fun Day in partnership with Wybourn Works.

Held across the Hub and Wybourn Community Primary School yard, the event brought the community together for a brilliant day of family fun. There were stalls, a bouncy castle, activities and plenty of food served from the Hub.

We were treated to lovely weather and an amazing turnout — the event was so popular that we even had to restock the food partway through the day!

It was wonderful to see so many local families and residents enjoying themselves and making the most of everything on offer.

A huge thank you to Wybourn Works, Wybourn Community Primary School, everyone who volunteered or ran a stall, and all those who came along and made the day such a fantastic success.

posts.title: Mother's Day Afternoon Tea at the Hub
posts.summary:
On Sunday 15 March 2026, we hosted a lovely Mother's Day Afternoon Tea at Pat Midgley Community Hub, bringing families, friends, and local residents together for a warm and welcoming celebration.

The afternoon was filled with tea, sweet treats, friendly conversation, and a chance to spend quality time together in the heart of the community. Events like this are a simple but important way for people to connect, relax, and celebrate special occasions close to home.

Thank you to everyone who came along and helped make the afternoon so special. For more updates, photos, and future event news, please keep an eye on our Facebook page.

posts.title: Summer recap 2024
posts.summary:
Over the summer the Pat Midgley Community Hub has provided an array of activities for the local community including a board games cafe, Pinders dance session, arts and crafts sessions with Ignite Imaginations, visual arts organisations and other local crafters including Lydia and Hayley.

These sessions were very popular with families, who got to design their own coasters, pencil cases and create clay models.

We're very grateful to our local partners, Manor & Castle Development Trust and MASKK to deliver the drop-in on Fridays and Wybourn Youth Hangout drop-ins - these truly make a difference during the long summer holidays. Many who came were our customers and other residents of Wybourn of all ages, many of them regularly attending weekly events at the centre.

One customer who attended for the first time for the event commented that it's 'a lovely community centre to get involved in'.

posts.title: Celebrating inspirational women
posts.summary:
A fantastic community event was held at the Pat Midgley Community Hub to mark International Women's Day.

Centre co-ordinator Christina Grant had her hands full on the night, as she organised and worked with multiple partner organisations to ensure the event was a big hit with women from the local community.

There were a variety of activities to take part in such as arts and crafts, free wellbeing checks by a nurse, and a variety of information and support from the council and Manor & Castle Development Trust, Wybourn Works and Great Places Housing Group.

Our customer Lydia, who Great Places supported to set up her graphic design business, set up an arts and crafts station and her business cards. Lydia's business relies heavily on word of mouth, so it was fantastic for her to get her business name out there and make connections to help her grow her business.

posts.title: Save Our UK Steel Campaign
posts.summary:
Unite the Union held their campaign in Wybourn to raise the profile of the village and the Pat Midgley Community Hub. This is a campaign to raise the profile of Wybourn.

There are a number of reasons why Wybourn was chosen, including the scenic views and the fact a number of steel workers live in the area. In this campaign, the Pat Midgley Community Hub was visible. Residents of Wybourn joined the campaign to help rally the "Save our steel" campaign.

posts.title: Christmas Grotto
posts.summary:
An elders' Christmas lunch was held for residents of Wybourn to bring together people who may be experiencing isolation during the Christmas period.

Councillor Laura Moynahan also joined us for the event and said "Lovely to join Pat Midgley Community Hub for a Christmas lunch with local residents."

posts.title: Halloween Spookiness!
posts.summary:
A party on Halloween night was well attended by local families. There was a range of activities on offer for the children including music, dancing and arts and crafts.

We were also joined by the wonderful and entertaining Barney Baloney, who kept the children laughing on the night!
